On the 22nd of May, 1992 a general mobilisation of Serbs was proclaimed. Vlado Vrkes was in charge, as well as Boro Savanovic and Boro Tadic. On the 25th of May, 1992 by orders of the Crisis Staff paramilitary units and the police arrest us, the leaders. They declare us to be Alija's fighters, Mujahedins, the worst extremists. In addition to us, other more -- men of repute in Sanski Most were arrested. We were taken to the prison at the Betonirka, the Hasan Kikic school, the Krings Hall. On the 26th of May in the evening paramilitary forces by decision of the Crisis Staff and the SDS carry out an armed attack on the town, shelling of the Muslim part of town Otoke, Muhici, and Gornja Mahala. On the 27th of May, I was taken away as well. In the course of the day of the 27th of May, there was evacuation and the beginning of systematic looting and burning of Otoke, Muhici, and Mahala. The people were gathered at the exercise grounds in Krkojevci. 43 victims were killed, women, children, and men, in Muhici and Mahala. Those victims several days later were collected and their bodies buried in a mass grave at Greda. On the 6th of June, 1992 by orders of the Crisis Staff the first group was taken to Manjaca. And from then on in certain time periods a total of some 1.500 men were taken to Manjaca. The transport was carried out in -- escorted by Serbian policemen upon instructions of Drago Vrucinic. That is all that I wrote down, and I allow this copy of mine to be photocopied -- this document to be photocopied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break now. Please, Mr. Biscevic, make that -- that block of notes available to the usher, who will make photocopies of it. Yes. He needs to come back because I want to know if there are any questions forthcoming and -- unfortunately. In the meantime, please Ms. Korner, Mr. Ackerman, and Mr. Zecevic, try to utilise the next 20, 30 minutes --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to talk to Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- because --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to find -- we need to find a solution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Otherwise I will have to impose a solution, which both of you will not like. I mean, as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At least that would be evenhanded, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Break for 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry for the delay, but we had a minor mishap. It was minor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sutherland informed me this morning she'd upset a whole pot of coffee over her desk, so I hope it wasn't as bad as that. Your Honours, we have spoken --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- and the Prosecution, as ever, has given in to this extent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a question of size.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, may be. Your Honour, I just hope that for future we can try and perhaps be a bit more agreeable on these matters, but anyhow, the agreement reached, subject to Your Honours' approval is this: that Mr. Ackerman, as he wishes to see Mr. Brdjanin tomorrow morning between 10.00, that will remain. We'd ask if Your Honours were to sit at 12.00 to start. Ms. Richterova, then depending on where she gets with her witnesses today, will complete those two witnesses, and then we'll deal with Charles McLeod. I would hope enough time being left that he can complete his evidence in chief. I'm pretty certain he can. And, Your Honour, then on Monday, cross-examination will take place in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go step-by-step. Tomorrow, you're suggesting that we commence at 12.00 noon.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, if that is agreeable to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but before -- do we have a courtroom available at 12.00?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. The Courtroom I will be available between 12.00 to 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That will mean sitting from 12.00 noon to what time?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry? Well, Your Honour, I'd ask the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have to advise me on this, because --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. From 12.00 until 6.30, the normal time, but just with two more breaks. A break for lunch, obviously.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So we can move between Courtroom I and Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But that's -- for me that is not a big problem. I mean, it's not a problem at all moving from one courtroom to another. But I still have to have the time. It's 12.00 noon until what time first before we break?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Just wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Everything is confused. I don't know how this happened, but my understanding of the agreement that I just made with Ms. Korner was this: That we were going to meet the entire day tomorrow, that I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just heard her say that she wants to honour your commitment to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. That commitment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- with Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. That commitment only has to do with meeting with him after he hears the tapes of the transcripts, which won't be available. So he can't hear them by tomorrow morning at 10.00. Therefore, it makes no sense for me to meet with him tomorrow morning at 10.00. It makes sense for me to meet with him Monday morning at 10.00, after he's had a chance to hear the tapes over the weekend, which is what my understanding was of what we were going to do. And so we can meet all day tomorrow, as far as I'm concerned, and finish up the two witnesses Ms. Richterova has plus the direct examination of Ms. Korner's witness, and then the cross-examination would be at the normal time Monday afternoon, and I think we can finish the cross-examination on Monday and that solves all the problems, and that was my understanding. I don't need to meet with Brdjanin tomorrow. I need to meet with him Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I understand that; in which case one -- we could sit -- I mean, I need to meet with Mr. McLeod, who's not arriving until this evening, as I said yesterday. But if we could -- I think if we could sit 10.00, then sit through until -- it may be I'll be finished at -- in fact we sit at 9.00 or 9.30, and then it may well be that if Your Honour feels --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me make myself clear. I still have to look right and left, because obviously, I mean, we haven't even started consulting amongst one another yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I would imagine that on the basis of past experience that there shouldn't be any problems. However, let's start. Are you suggesting that we start at 10.00, therefore?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. For Ms. Richterova to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I need to know exactly what time we would break after that. That would be 11.30?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For half an hour, resuming at 12.00 noon and finishing at 1.30. Then we would have a break of...?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour will obviously want, I imagine, a bit more for the luncheon adjournment. So if we said we sat again at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And depending on where we've got to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- we may need to move courts after that, but I would hope not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that would mean sitting till 4.00?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Although, I heard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically we're talking of an hour and a half here, another hour and a half here. That's three hours. And that's another hour and a half here. Four and a half hours, I think that should be plenty for one day. I wouldn't like -- even if you want to shorten it by quarter of an hour, I would be prepared to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, it's -- okay. So tentatively first proposition: 10.00 a.m. to 11.30, 12.00 to 1.30, 2.30 to 4.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that agreeable to the two Defence teams? Okay. So tomorrow that will be the time schedule. Madam Registrar, you're tasked with informing the parties -- the times are established but the courtrooms are not, so please -- Courtroom I to start with.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exactly. Just the last one, from 2.30 to 4.00, we'll be sitting in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In Courtroom II. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that seems to be the arrangement: Courtroom I until 1.30 and Courtroom II for the last -- the third and final session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Can I -- and there's one -- I've spoken to Mr. Ackerman and I've asked if it's possible that both sets of cross-examination could be completed on the Monday session in the afternoon. At the moment my intention is that he will start in Stakic then only on the Tuesday morning. But it may well be, because I haven't had a chance to address Judge Schomburg, that he may want him to start his examination-in-chief on the Monday before he's finished in this court. In that event, I'm taking it from what was raised earlier there's no objection, although it's a highly undesirable way of proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. But I interfere as little as I can in these things, as you may have gathered. But -- Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't force anyone to tell me beforehand either --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No objection to what? I don't --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's Mr. Ackerman's original suggestion that Mr. McLeod should start his examination-in-chief in the Stakic case before he's being cross-examined in this case. I hope that's not going to happen, but it may well be that's what has to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I don't have any objection to that happening. I think, you know -- I am certain that he is a very busy man, and I think his time here should be utilised to the fullest if possible. So I don't have an objection to his spending some time in Stakic in the midst of what we're doing here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whether he can do it is another matter, but anyhow ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So anyway, we'll start from that. So the understanding as far as tomorrow is concerned, it's all clear. And then Monday we'll reassess the situation obviously, and we will do our -- our level best to finish with the witness so that -- we'll try anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Your Honour. Thank you very much, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, are you sure you want to put questions to the witness on the statement that he read or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Actually, I have five questions for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And Mr. Ackerman -- or Mr. Trbojevic, do you want to put questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, do you intend to put questions to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. My only suggestion would be, I think, if these -- if his statement is treated as evidence, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. It's not going to -- I'm not going to treat it as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not going to treat it as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In that case, I don't honestly see the need. I've put all my questions to him. They put all their questions to him. The Chamber allowed him to make his statement, which is not evidence. You're not a lay jury. If it's not treated as evidence, I don't see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, I have no intention of admitting this as evidence. Obviously you have a copy of it. If there is a request from one of you to have it admitted as evidence, we will consider it. But frankly, I mean, it's -- I don't ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not trying to stop you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not trying to stop you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I know that you're not trying to stop me. And the point is that his statement is on the transcript, so we have now a couple -- this is not the statement. These are the facts, the dates, the actual names of the people. That is why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Bring the witness in again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I mean, this is going to be considered anyhow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But my invitation to you was to pre-assess where this could -- where you could get with these five questions, whether it's going to change anything or --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. I know it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just as much as his extra statement, whether it has changed anything or not from his previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My point, Your Honour, if I may, is that if the statement which he read at the end after I was through with my redirect examination, if that's not evidence, there's no point in him questioning. The answers won't be evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He made a statement in open court. That -- he made a statement. And what's not going to be evidence is this -- these notes which I suppose include also the version -- the written version or the prepared statement that he read from. I mean, I don't -- I don't need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He made a statement verbally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My only suggestion was that his statement made here be treated as just a statement made - it wasn't a response to questioning - and that it not be considered in your deliberations either way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But Your Honours, with all due respect, this statement was made in the open court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have every right to question him, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And that is why -- and the witness has provided with new information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That has been pointed out. Yeah, especially as regards date, because you put questions to him during your cross-examination regarding the dates and it's obvious that you are not agreeing. Try to be as short -- concise as you can so that we get it over and done with.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Biscevic, as a result of you reading your -- your reading of that short statement that you made, Mr. Zecevic has got a few questions to -- additional questions to put to you, so please listen to what he needs to question you about and give us a short answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Biscevic, just a few questions for clarification in connection with this statement of yours. In your statement, you repeated that the arrival of the 6th Krajina Brigade occurred on the 14th of March. And yesterday I thought we had agreed that it was on the 3rd of April.

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read out what I had noted down. And we agreed you are probably right. I will not dispute the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in your statement you mentioned -- I think on page 44 of the transcript - I don't want to waste time by quoting you - you mentioned members of the Crisis Staff, I think.

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the investigators of the Prosecution in 1997 and 1999, on page 00838012, second paragraph of the English version, you said the following. And I'll quote you in English: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... "the Crisis Staff as the authority they had to consult but never specifically stated who were the members of the Crisis Staff. At that time I did not know who were the members of the Serb Crisis Staff in Sanski Most." [Interpretation] Did you make that statement?

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This statement that you made today was based on what? When you listed members of the Crisis Staff when in your statement to the investigator, you explicitly said that you didn't know who were members of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are my notes that I took down every day on the basis of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you learnt about these facts as to who were members of the Crisis Staff after 1999?

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So I assume someone told you.

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in contact with others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, these questions could have been asked on his original cross-examination. They're all based on this statement. It's got nothing to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we'll finish earlier if you let Mr. Zecevic finish with his five questions. I think you have already put four.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I have two or three more, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your statement today, you said that on the 19th of April, the Crisis Staff was formed by the SDS, SOS, and the 6th Brigade, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this is some other Crisis Staff, if I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this, too, is something you learnt after 1999.

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are my notes that I work on on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Today -- or, rather, yesterday and today, you repeated that on the 20th of April -- that it is true that on the 20th of April, according to what you know, General Talic came to the meeting, and that on that occasion he said to Mr. Kurbegovic that what had been done in Sanski Most was wrong and that Rasula had done it on his own initiative. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in your statement, you said that the mobilisation took place on the 22nd of May and that it was organised by Vlado Vrkes, Boro Savanovic, and Boro Tadic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Vlado Vrkes was the President of the SDS, Boro Savanovic President of the Club of Deputies, and Boro Tadic a member of the SDA, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So not one of them was a military man.

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were civilians who later put on uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me one more thing. From your notes here, I can see that you know Adil Draganovic, a Judge of the court in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: FAIK BISCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This you could have asked him before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean it's -- you don't need to see one's notes to know -- and he told you that. He mentioned Adil Draganovic earlier. He said that Adil Draganovic was in Manjaca. So he mentioned him already.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is just the information which we got right now. This is new information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which information?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That Draganovic Adil was the organiser of the SDA party in Sanski Most. This is relevant information which we received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So ask him the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Adil Draganovic was the organiser --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This isn't about the statement now that he made just before he finished on his own. As you said, Adil Draganovic was mentioned in his direct examination. There is -- I don't see any point in asking questions about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think I'm going to stop you Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, if I may say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because these notes, he made them available not because he referred to them. He made them available because he wanted to make them available. But I allowed you to question further the witness on the basis of what he stated in his final statement and not beyond that, not beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours, but with all due respect, we have found a piece of information right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's your problem. That's your problem. Ask some other witness, not him. With this witness, you can ask him with regard to the statement that he made. In his final statement, he did not mention Adil Draganovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So, Mr. Biscevic, that brings us to the end of your role here as a witness. On behalf of the other two Judges and the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for having come here to give evidence. You will now be escorted by the usher, and you will be given all the assistance you require to return to your home. I thank you once more, and you may now withdraw. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much and good-bye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And have a safe journey. Next witness. We'll give the usher a chance to escort the first witness out.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This witness is in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The witness is in closed session, so we will go --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The next witness, BT14, is in closed session. So we will wait for the usher to come forward and prepare the courtroom for a closed session, according to the Rules.
